_: Austenitic stainless steel AISI 304 (18Cr-8Ni, UNS S30400), annealed, at room temperature, brushed (No. 4) finish unless a state says otherwise: railings, sinks, appliances, cutlery, tools, fittings. A carbon / structural steel state (S235 / A36) changes density, conductivity and adds rust. Partners research lane 11-07 (the project's materials research note PARTNERS.md).

alpha.src: brushed Ra 0.4-1 um with directional grooves (anisotropic: alpha ~0.08 along, ~0.3 across the brush lines); mirror Ra < 0.05 um; bead-blast Ra 1-3 um; practice, no measured BRDF fit found

n.src: JC74_FE data file re-read 11-08 (refractiveindex.info database main/Fe/nk/Johnson.yml, CC0): 0.549 um n 2.95 k 2.93, 0.582 um n 2.94 k 2.99, so n 2.95, k 2.93 at 550 nm (iron; 304 is Fe-Cr-Ni, its n,k within ~10 %); corrected from n 2.87, k 3.35

F0.src: ((n-1)^2 + k^2)/((n+1)^2 + k^2) at 550 nm with n 2.95, k 2.93 (recomputed 11-08 after the n,k correction; was 0.562): a conductor, the specular colour IS the base colour, no diffuse

F0_rgb.src: stainless steel reflectance near-neutral, a hair warmer than aluminium (PBR practice tables, consistent with the n,k above)

anisotropy.v: brushed finish: highlight stretched across the brush direction

n_k_550nm.src: JC74_FE data file re-read 11-08 (refractiveindex.info database main/Fe/nk/Johnson.yml, CC0): 0.549 um n 2.95 k 2.93, 0.582 um n 2.94 k 2.99, so n 2.95, k 2.93 at 550 nm (iron; 304 is Fe-Cr-Ni, its n,k within ~10 %); corrected from n 2.87, k 3.35

absorption.v: opaque metal: light absorbed within ~15 nm (skin depth lambda/(4 pi k)); no subsurface scattering
absorption.src: lambda/(4 pi k) = 550 nm/(4 pi 2.93) = 15 nm (recomputed 11-08 with the re-read k)

static.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: steel on steel clean and dry 0.5-0.8, grease 0.16, lard 0.11, graphite 0.058; dry_air_exposed [0.4, 0.6] and the lubricated 0.1 E; MARKS mild steel 0.74 E: recalled from Marks' Handbook, not re-read; stainless on stainless galls (adhesive wear) when clean and loaded

kinetic.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: steel on steel clean and dry 0.42, castor oil 0.081, lard 0.084 (lubricated 0.05-0.1 E around them); MARKS mild steel 0.57 E: recalled from Marks' Handbook, not re-read

friction.counterface: steel on steel (pairs/partners.json holds aluminium, rubber.sole, plastic.comb, wood, glass, ice; pairs/skin.json holds skin)

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: MANTEL94: the surface energy of 304 foil decays with the hydrocarbon overlayer thickness, not the oxide type; a clean oxide is high-energy (water spreads); within hours in air it reads like a polymer

tack.v: none dry; flat oiled or wet plates hold by capillarity (Laplace pressure ~ 2 gamma / gap)

restitution.src: E: recalled from Goldsmith 1960 (GOLDSMITH60), not re-read: GOLDSMITH60 steel on steel 0.9-0.95 low speed; ARYAEI10 e falls as the ball grows and the sheet softens

collision_thickness_mm.src: numerical offset only: a rigid solid has no compliant surface layer; 0.1 mm as the glass/stone profiles (below screen-readable gap, above field step resolution)

E_star_GPa.src: E / (1 - nu^2) from E 193 GPa, nu 0.29 (half-space modulus; the soft partner's own E* combines in series)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: flat punch k = 2 E* a over area pi a^2, a 50 mm (hand-sized patch): an unyielding barrier next to any soft partner

hertz_constant_N_per_m1_5_R25mm.src: F = (4/3) E* sqrt(R) d^1.5, rigid sphere R 25 mm

contact_damping_ratio.src: zeta = -ln e / sqrt(pi^2 + ln^2 e) from restitution 0.9

restitution.src: E: recalled from Goldsmith 1960 (GOLDSMITH60), not re-read: GOLDSMITH60 hardened steel spheres on steel blocks e ~0.9-0.95 at low speed (drops with size and speed as plasticity starts; ARYAEI10)

response_time_ms.src: Hertz contact time t = 2.87 (m^2/(R E*^2 v))^0.2, rigid 1 kg sphere, R 25 mm, 1 m/s: sub-millisecond; in a slap or a step the soft partner sets the pulse

damping_ratio.src: as contact_damping_ratio (energy lost per impact, from restitution)

solver._: Rigid next to any body tissue; it dents (yields at 215 MPa) only under point loads far above anything a body applies. Sheet and tube ring when struck: the ring is the bar/plate modes at these wave speeds with very low damping (zeta ~1e-4 internal; the 0.034 here is the contact loss).

water_contact_angle_deg.src: US8453425 bare stainless steel 62.6 deg (66.3 after a fuel wipe); FORREST15: on real metal surfaces the angle is set by a ~5 nm hydrocarbon overlayer

wetting._: Water beads on handled steel (fingerprint sebum raises the angle to 80-90) and sheets on freshly cleaned steel.

v.position: conductor: the zero of the scale; it takes charge from hair (+45), skin (+30), nylon (+30) and gives it to rubber (SBR -35, NR -105), PP (-90), PTFE (-190); grounded steel bleeds any charge at once

triboelectric.src: ALPHALAB: all conductors about the same affinity (the table's zero); metal rubbing is pressure-dependent and can reverse

resistivity_ohm_m.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): electrical resistivity 7.2e-005 ohm-cm (72 uohm cm)

v.isolated_object: holds charge on its capacitance (a few pF for a hand tool) until it touches a conductor: the spark from a door handle is the body's charge, not the steel's

permittivity_rel.src: not defined for a conductor (fully screening)

hardness.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): HB 123, HRB 70, HV 129 (HB and HV converted from Rockwell B by the sheet); Mohs E from practice

abrasion.v: scratched by quartz sand (Mohs 7) in grit; brushed finishes hide wear, mirror finishes show swirl marks; galling between clean stainless pairs

density_kg_m3.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 8 g/cc (MIF 7.8-8.0)

E_GPa.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 193-200 GPa; 193 kept (MIF 200)

poisson.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 0.29 (MIF 0.28)

yield_MPa.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 0.2 % offset yield 215 MPa; ASTM A240 min 205 and cold work 500-1000 E: recalled, not re-read

ultimate_MPa.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 505 MPa

elongation_pct.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 70 % in 50 mm (annealed): bends and dents, does not snap

hardening.v: strong work hardening (austenitic): a bent sheet stiffens at the bend

toughness_KIC_MPa_m05.src: austenitic stainless fails by ductile tearing; K_IC is not valid-measurable at room temperature in thin sections; J-integral equivalents > 100 MPa m^0.5 (fracture mechanics practice)

thermal_expansion_1_K.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): CTE 17.3 um/m-C at 20 C (0-100 C); 17.8 at 250 C, 18.7 at 500 C

sim._: Rigid for every body contact; elastoplastic only for props that bend (thin sheet, wire).

conductivity_W_mK.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 16.2 W/m-K at 0-100 C (21.5 at 500 C; the src said 'at 100 C') (MIF 16)

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 0.5 J/g-C (MIF 480 J/kgK)

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) = sqrt(16.2 x 8000 x 500) W s^0.5 m^-2 K^-1

contact_temp_with_skin_C.src: SKINTH: T = (e_skin 33 + e 20)/(e_skin + e), skin 33 C on material 20 C, e_skin 1188; lower = feels colder

emissivity.src: EMIS_ETB re-read 11-08: stainless polished 0.075, weathered 0.85, type 301 0.54-0.63; mirror 0.07 kept; brushed 0.1-0.2 E between; the oxidised lower bound 0.8 E (the table's 0.85 row says weathered, not oxidised)

thermal_expansion_1_K.src: ASM_304 datasheet re-read 11-08 (ASM / MatWeb sheet MQ304A, PDF at aerospacemetals.com): 17.3 um/m-C (0-100 C)

wet.src: a water film on steel: steel-steel between dry and lubricated; skin on wet steel grips MORE (pairs/skin.json, skin hydration), rubber soles grip less (pairs/partners.json)

oily.src: ETB friction table re-read 11-08: steel on steel grease 0.16 (MARKS greasy 0.16, recalled, agrees); an oil film raises the water angle (beads, E)

polished_mirror.src: mirror No. 8 finish; low emissivity (EMIS_ETB); EMIS_ETB re-read 11-08: stainless polished 0.075

carbon_steel.src: E: recalled from ASM / EN 10025 typical values, not re-read: structural steel S235 / ASTM A36: density 7850, E 200 GPa, yield 235-250 MPa, k ~50 W/mK, c ~490 (ASM / EN 10025 typical); effusivity D sqrt(k rho c), feels colder than stainless (contact ~20.4 C)

rusted.src: carbon steel only: iron oxide-hydroxide (rust) is a porous rough dielectric (orange-brown diffuse albedo, n ~2.0-2.3), not a metal; friction and emissivity rise (EMIS_ETB oxidised iron 0.6-0.9); the EMIS_ETB iron rows were not re-read 11-08

cold.src: at -10 C the contact temperature with skin is about -4.5 C (effusivity 8050 vs skin 1188): wet skin can freeze to it (stuck-tongue effect) because heat is pulled from the contact faster than skin supplies it

ETB.cite: The Engineering ToolBox, Friction and friction coefficients for some common materials
ETB.lic: free web reference; numbers used as facts (friction table re-read 11-08)

MARKS.cite: Marks' Standard Handbook for Mechanical Engineers, friction coefficient table (static/kinetic, dry and greasy, metals on metals)
MARKS.lic: paywalled handbook; numbers used as facts (recalled from the source, not re-read 11-07)

ALPHALAB.cite: Lee B / AlphaLab Inc. (TriField) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J (positive = charges +); zero = the average conductor (all metals about equal); read via the storiesinfabric.blogspot.com reprint 11-07
ALPHALAB.lic: free web table, reproduction only in whole: single numbers used as facts, table not copied STUDY ONLY (P13)

SKINTH.cite: skin thermal inputs for contact temperature: k 0.37 W/mK, c 3500 J/kgK (Duck 1990 tissue tables, typical), rho 1090 from skin.body

ASM_304.cite: ASM Aerospace Specification Metals / MatWeb, AISI Type 304 Stainless Steel datasheet (annealed): density 8.00, E 193 GPa, nu 0.29, yield 215 MPa, UTS 505 MPa, elongation 70 %, HB 123, k 16.2 W/mK, c 500 J/kgK, CTE 17.3e-6/K, resistivity 72 uohm cm
ASM_304.lic: MatWeb terms forbid redistributing the data compilation: single numbers used as facts, STUDY ONLY (P13); re-read 11-08: every number above matches; the sheet also lists shear modulus 86 GPa (its own E and nu give 74.8)

MIF.cite: MakeItFrom.com, AISI 304 (S30400) Stainless Steel: density 7.8 g/cm3, E 200 GPa, nu 0.28, c 480 J/kgK, k 16 W/mK
MIF.lic: copyrighted web compilation: numbers used as facts, table not copied STUDY ONLY (P13)

JC74_FE.cite: Johnson PB, Christy RW. Optical constants of transition metals: Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Pd. Phys Rev B 9:5056 (1974), via refractiveindex.info; data file re-read 11-08 (refractiveindex.info-database main/Fe/nk/Johnson.yml)
JC74_FE.lic: refractiveindex.info CC0; numbers used as facts

GOLDSMITH60.cite: Goldsmith W. Impact: the theory and physical behaviour of colliding solids. Edward Arnold (1960): restitution tables for steel spheres
GOLDSMITH60.lic: book; numbers used as facts (recalled from the source, not re-read 11-07)

ARYAEI10.cite: Aryaei A, Hashemnia K, Jafarpur K. Experimental and numerical study of ball size effect on restitution coefficient in low velocity impacts. Int J Impact Eng 37:1037-1044 (2010)
ARYAEI10.lic: paywalled; finding (e falls with ball size, rises with sheet hardness) used

US8453425.cite: US Patent 8,453,425, Soot reduction by combustor conditioning: example water contact angle on bare stainless steel 62.6 deg, 66.3 deg after a Jet A wipe
US8453425.lic: US patent, public domain text; number used as a fact

MANTEL94.cite: Mantel M, Wightman JP. Influence of the surface chemistry on the wettability of stainless steel. Surf Interface Anal 21:595-605 (1994)

FORREST15.cite: Forrest E et al. / Sandia: Influence of surface contamination on the wettability of heat transfer surfaces (2015): water angle on cleaned metal set by a ~5 nm hydrocarbon overlayer

EMIS_ETB.cite: The Engineering ToolBox, Emissivity coefficients of common products (re-read 11-08: stainless polished 0.075, weathered 0.85, type 301 0.54-0.63; aluminum highly polished 0.039-0.057, commercial sheet 0.09, rough 0.07, anodized 0.77; rubber hard glossy plate 0.94, natural hard 0.91, natural soft 0.86; plastics 0.90-0.97; no nylon row)
EMIS_ETB.lic: free web reference; numbers used as facts (re-read 11-08)
